title: D-010: Source-of-Truth Discipline
body:
# D-010: Source-of-Truth Discipline

**Date:** 2026-03-28
**Status:** Active

## Decision

The framework repo (this repo) is the canonical source of doctrine, commands, agents, style packs, workflows, and schemas. Other repos may extend locally but must not silently drift. Sync mechanisms are core features, not optional extras.

## Why

Without source-of-truth discipline, the framework fragments. Each repo ends up with a different version of doctrine, incompatible schemas, or conflicting style pack definitions. The sync system (Phase 6) exists specifically to prevent and detect this drift.

Drift is the primary long-term threat to a portable framework. In the short term, a repo with a slightly outdated style pack or a slightly different schema version will appear to work correctly — agents run, documents are produced, QA passes. The failure appears later, when: a schema change in the source framework breaks a consuming agent in a dependent repo; a doctrine update in the source framework contradicts the behavior of an agent in a dependent repo that loaded the old doctrine; two dependent repos produce documents with different quality standards because they have diverged from the same source.

By declaring source-of-truth discipline as a core principle and implementing sync mechanisms as Phase 6 deliverables (not optional additions), the framework commits to treating drift as a first-class quality concern.

## Key Rule from Doctrine

"Import/export and sync mechanisms are core features, not optional extras." This was declared non-negotiable in the architecture spec. The sync/ directory, sync_manifest schema, and /sync-framework command are all first-class Phase 6 deliverables.

## Local Extensions

Local extensions are valid and expected. A dependent repo may:
- Add world-specific canon records for a D&D campaign
- Add organization-specific style pack extensions for an internal documentation standard
- Add domain-specific guide records for a specialized subject area

Local extensions that do not conflict with framework content are explicitly permitted. Local extensions that modify or override framework-level doctrine, schemas, or canonical commands are B8 (canon conflict) blockers requiring explicit user decision.

## Alternatives Considered

**Forking:** Each repo takes a full copy of the framework and modifies it independently. Rejected: produces guaranteed divergence with no mechanism for reconciliation. Forks cannot be synced without manual comparison.

**No sync mechanism (copy-on-install only):** Install the framework once and accept that dependent repos will drift over time. Rejected: the framework's value is in its doctrine and schemas, both of which will evolve as the framework matures. Dependent repos that cannot receive updates cannot benefit from improvements.

## Consequences

The sync/ directory, sync_manifest schema, and /sync-framework, /export-pack, /import-pack, and /install-framework commands are all Phase 6 deliverables. Phase 6 is the last phase precisely because portability is built on top of a fully implemented framework — you cannot make something portable until you know what it is.
